newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Imran Khan demands death penalty for corruption.
newsitem.headline: Imran Khan demands death penalty for corruption.

text.p: Pakistani cricketer- turned-politician Imram Khan said on Saturday his party wanted the death penalty for corruption.

"I believe it's about time that strict punishment should be given to people involved in corruption. There should be capital punishment for such people," he told a news conference to kick off his election drive in the southern port city of Karachi.
President Farooq Leghari set National Assembly elections for February 3 after ousting Benazir Bhutto's government on November 5 on disputed allegations of misrule and corruption.
Leghari issued an ordinance last month setting up an Accountability Commission to investigate charges of corruption against people holding public office.

"This is not fascism," Imran said when asked to comment on his advocacy of execution by people for those convicted of corruption. "We will not do this arbitrarily. We will do this through the democratic process, through the judicial process."

Imran said his party supported Leghari's moves to establish an anti-corruption process, but added that should not exclude the head of state, judges and military officers as at present. "We stand for across-the-board accountability," he said.

Imran, who launched his Tehreek-e-Insaaf (Justice Movement) in April, said he had no source of income currently, but had paid 400,000 rupees (about $10,000) in wealth tax on his assets during the year.

"At the moment I am selling my assets to survive," said the former Pakistani cricket captain, who married Anglo-French heiress Jemima Goldsmith last year. He said he planned to rent out his apartment in Islamabad to help make ends meet.
